title: Personal Fall Arrest System Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.502)
subtitle: For supervisors checking fall protection on a construction site before and during work at height.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
When an item fails, remove the defective component from service, and don't let work that needs that protection start until it is corrected.
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Harness, lanyards and lifelines
items: Harness, lanyard, lifeline and connectors checked before this use; no wear, damage or other deterioration found
Any worn, damaged or deteriorated component removed from service
Harness, not body belt, for fall arrest
Every worker on a personal fall arrest system wears a body harness; no body belt is part of the arrest system
Lanyard or lifeline connected at the center of the back near shoulder level, or above the head
Equipment that has arrested a fall
No impact-loaded harness, lanyard or connector in use unless a competent person inspected it and found it undamaged and suitable for reuse
Lifelines run clear of sharp edges or are protected; no cuts or abrasion on the line
Each worker on a separate vertical lifeline, unless every elevator shaft condition in 1926.502(d)(10)(ii) is met
Rope and webbing in lanyards, lifelines and harness strength straps are synthetic fiber
Harnesses, lanyards and components not used to lift or lower materials

sections.title: Connectors and snaphooks
items: Every snaphook in use is a locking type

No snaphook clipped directly to webbing, rope or wire rope, to another snaphook, to a D-ring already holding another connector, to a horizontal lifeline, or to an object that could open the keeper, unless the locking hook is designed for that connection
Connectors are drop forged, pressed or formed steel, or an equivalent material
Corrosion-resistant finish; no rough surfaces or sharp edges that could damage webbing or other parts
Manufacturer data shows a rated tensile strength of 5,000 pounds or more
Label or manufacturer data shows breaking strength of 5,000 pounds or more
Self-retracting devices limiting free fall to 2 feet
Devices that limit free fall to 2 feet or less are rated to sustain 3,000 pounds or more with the line fully extended
Other self-retracting devices and energy-absorbing lanyards
Self-retracting devices that don't limit free fall to 2 feet or less, ripstitch lanyards, and tearing and deforming lanyards are rated to sustain 5,000 pounds or more with the line fully extended
Where a horizontal lifeline can become vertical, the connecting device locks in both directions

sections.title: Anchorage, rigging and rescue
items: Required fall protection installed before the worker starts the task that exposes them to the fall
Anchor independent of any platform support or suspension anchor and rated for 5,000 pounds per worker attached, or engineered under qualified-person supervision as 1926.502(d)(15)(i) and (ii) set out
Anchor height and lanyard length keep free fall to 6 feet or less, and the worker cannot contact any lower level during an arrest
Lifeline designed, installed and used under a qualified person's supervision, as part of a complete personal fall arrest system that keeps a safety factor of at least two
No tie-off to guardrails or hoists
No lanyard or lifeline attached to a guardrail; none attached to a hoist unless another subpart allows it
At hoist areas the system lets the worker reach the edge of the walking/working surface and no farther
Prompt rescue arrangements in place for a fallen worker, or workers able to rescue themselves

sections.title: Guardrails
items: Top edge measures 42 inches, plus or minus 3 inches, from the deck (raised by stilt height where stilts are used)
Midrail, screen, mesh or intermediate members present wherever there is no wall or parapet at least 21 inches high
Midrail halfway between the top edge and the walking/working level
No opening in the guardrail system more than 19 inches wide
No steel or plastic banding used as a top rail or midrail
Top rails and midrails at least one-quarter inch nominal diameter or thickness
Wire rope top rails flagged with high-visibility material at no more than 6-foot intervals
No splinters, burrs or points that could puncture or cut a worker or snag clothing
Guardrail on every unprotected side or edge of the hole
Chain, gate or removable section across the access opening whenever hoisting is not taking place

sections.title: Hole covers and safety nets
items: Cover fixed in place so wind, equipment or workers cannot shift it
Cover color coded or marked HOLE or COVER (cast iron manhole covers and steel street grates excepted)
Cover supports at least twice the weight of workers, equipment and materials that may be on it at one time
Cover supports at least twice the maximum axle load of the largest vehicle expected to cross
Net as close as practicable below the work surface and no more than 30 feet below it
Net inspected within the last week and after any event that could affect it; no wear, damage or deterioration
Drop test done after installation and before use, after relocation or major repair, and within 6 months if left in one place
Where drop-testing is unreasonable, the latest signed certification record for this net and installation is at the jobsite
No materials, scrap, equipment or tools left in the net; anything that fell in cleared before the next shift

references: 29 CFR 1926.502: Fall protection systems criteria and practices (Part 1926 Subpart M: Fall Protection)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
